title: Operations Rule on Improper Parking and Unreturned Vehicles, Wayfare Bikes and Scooters
content:
**Improper parking.** A Wayfare Bikes and Scooters vehicle ended outside a station or parking zone is charged the plan's improper parking fee, except that, where the plan's first-offense setting gives a warning, the rider's first improper parking within the plan's parking lookback period gets a warning instead of the fee.

**Unreturned vehicle.** A ride not ended the plan's lost-vehicle threshold of elapsed hours after unlock is charged the plan's lost vehicle fee for the type of vehicle not returned.

## Judging the first offense

The lookback period is the plan's lookback number of calendar months ending on the date of the ride. Counted in it are the rider's improper parking fees and first-offense parking warnings, on all of the rider's Wayfare Bikes and Scooters plans together, not only the plan the ride is under. An improper parking with no earlier fee or warning counted in the period is the rider's first, and gets the warning; one with any earlier fee or warning counted in the period is charged the fee.

| Earlier improper parking of the same rider (the only one) | Falls within the lookback period | Result for the present improper parking |
|---|---|---|
| none | — | warning instead of the fee |
| a fee, on the same plan | yes | improper parking fee |
| a warning, on another plan of the same rider | yes | improper parking fee |
| a fee, before the lookback period began | no | warning instead of the fee |

## What is booked

- An improper parking fee is one entry per ride improperly ended, recording the moment of unlock and the vehicle ridden.
- A lost vehicle fee is one entry per ride not ended, recording the moment of unlock and the vehicle not returned; the fee is the one for that vehicle type.

## Hypothetical cases

Taking, for illustration, a lookback of 12 months and a threshold of 24 hours:

1. A rider ends a scooter outside any parking zone on 20 September. The rider's only earlier warning was on 2 July of the same year, on a different plan. That warning lies within the 12 months ending on 20 September, so the present one is charged the fee.
2. Another rider's only earlier improper parking fee was 15 months before the ride. It lies outside the lookback period; the present improper parking is the first within the period and gets a warning.
3. A classic bike unlocked at 08:00 on a Tuesday is still not ended at 09:00 on the Wednesday: 25 elapsed hours have passed, beyond 24, and the ride is charged the lost vehicle fee for a classic bike. Had the bike been ended at 20:00 on the Tuesday, 12 hours after unlock, the threshold would not have been reached.
